subject: Seacliff Therapeutics — on-prem K8s consolidation & IO topology review
messages:
From: Emma Li <emma.li@seaclifftx.com>

Cc: procurement@seaclifftx.com
Date: Mon, 20 Apr 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Seacliff on-prem consolidation intake

Hi Chloe,

Thanks for taking this on. We're starting a program to consolidate two legacy inference clusters into a single Seacliff-managed on-prem Kubernetes footprint. High level:
- Primary workloads: low-latency inference endpoints (streaming & sync), nightly batch reranking jobs, embeddings backfill jobs.
- Current env: 12 GPU nodes (mixed V100/P100), 18 CPU nodes for batch, local NVMe on 6 nodes, central SAN for long-term artifacts.
- Availability target: 99.9% for API endpoints; 95th / 99th latency targets matter for certain models.
- Data residency: everything must stay inside our VPC; backups can cross to an approved S3-compatible object store inside our region.

I've attached an inventory spreadsheet with node names and rough I/O profiles (seacliff-inventory-v1.xlsx). Can you review and suggest an initial node pool layout and storage topology? Also need a sense of rollout risk — we're constrained on rack space and would prefer a minimal control plane footprint.

Emma
Emma Li
Head of Infrastructure, Seacliff Therapeutics
emma.li@seaclifftx.com
+1 415-555-0124

Subject: Re: Seacliff on-prem consolidation intake

Hi Emma — thanks for the inventory. We've had a quick look and can absolutely help consolidate this. Before we size nodepools and commit to control plane counts, two quick asks:

1) Workload profile: typical QPS per endpoint (p95/p99 goals) and batch concurrency for nightly jobs.
2) KV/cache behavior: do you use large prefix KH caches or small per-request caches? This changes ephemeral NVMe sizing.
3) Retention/backups: how long do you need model artifacts retained in object storage? Do you have a daily snapshot window?

Preliminary proposal (high level):
- 3 control plane nodes (HA) if you can spare them, otherwise a 1-control plan with etcd standby for very constrained racks — we'll walk options.
- Nodepools: gpu-heavy (inference 1: 4 x A100-equivalent per pool), gpu-ephemeral (local NVMe for KV cache), cpu-workers (batch/backfills), infra (logging/metrics + storage gateway).
- Storage: local NVMe for KV/cache, blockstore (SAN or regional block) for model artifacts and persistent metadata, object store for backups.

I'll loop in Aditya (runtime/serving) and Neha (networking/egress) to scope egress, firewall, and storage network topology. Can we set a 45-min call tomorrow to run through the details? If you prefer we can sketch a conservative nodepool layout first and iterate.

Best,
Chloe Martin

Emma / Chloe — adding some concrete starting points based on the inventory and our field experience. These are conservative, we'll tighten after the call and an IO profile pass.

Suggested initial nodepool matrix:
- control-plane: 3 x m5.large-ish (or equivalent baremetal: 8 vCPU / 32GB) with local SSD for etcd snapshots (RAID-1 recommended); keep them on separate racks where possible.
- gpu-inference: 4 nodes per pool, each with 4 x A100-80GB (or 8 x A100-40GB equivalent), 1TB nvme local for model cache + swap; 2 pools to enable canary rollouts.
- gpu-ephemeral-cache: 2 nodes with high NVMe (4TB total each), pinned to latency-critical shard locations for KV cache.
- cpu-batch: autoscaling group: min 6 / max 20 depending on nightly concurrency; attached to blockstore via multipath iSCSI or similar.
- infra: 3 nodes for logging, metrics, and storage gateway — separate from batch workers.

Storage topology notes:
- Keep model artifacts on replicated blockstore (multi-AZ if you have regional replication) with mount-to-read-only on inference nodes. Use local NVMe as a writable cache for KV and transient activations.
- Backups: daily snapshot to S3-compatible object store; retention 30 days by default (configurable).
- Encryption: KMS integration for object and blockstore.

Networking / egress considerations (Neha to expand): ensure pod egress to object store is via a NAT gateway in the VPC; control plane endpoints limited to management VLAN; BGP to backbone if they need peering.

I'll attach a nodepool proposal PDF with node-level hardware SKU suggestions and rough cost delta (redwood-nodepool-proposal-v1.pdf).

—Aditya
Aditya Rao

Thanks Aditya — this is helpful. A few details to help you refine:
- Target traffic: 600 QPS aggregate for public inference endpoints, p95 latency target 120ms, p99 300ms for the top model.
- Batch: nightly embeddings backfill runs at 200 concurrent workers, prefers spot preemptible capacity if available.
- KV/cache profile: mostly small keys (~1-8KB) with high read:write ratio (10:1); hotset ~150GB, warmset ~800GB.
- Retention: model artifacts retained 90 days; logs retained 180 days.
- Encryption: must use our HSM-backed KMS (we'll give details during onboarding).

Attached a quick storage sketch (seacliff-storage-sketch-v1.png) showing two racks with mixed NVMe and a SAN head. Rack constraints: only 2U per rack free for additional GPUs — that will limit immediate scale.

We can do the call tomorrow 10:00am PT. Please confirm proposed meeting link and agenda.

Emma

Subject: Re: Seacliff on-prem consolidation intake

Emma — thanks for the additional numbers, that clarifies a lot. Quick summary of what we'll deliver before the 10:00am call:

1) Topology proposal (PDF): 3 control-plane nodes (HA) with etcd on dedicated SSDs; 2 GPU inference pools (4 nodes each) to enable staged rollouts; 1 small gpu-ephemeral-cache pool (2 nodes) specifically for KV hotset; CPU batch autoscaling group for nightly workloads.

2) Storage layout: local NVMe for the 150GB hotset (replicated across the two ephemeral-cache nodes), model artifacts on blockstore with read-only mounts to inference nodes, daily snapshots to your S3-compatible store with 90-day retention. We'll propose snapshot window to avoid batch backup collisions.

3) Networking & compliance: control plane management VLAN, nodepools in isolated tenant VLANs, egress via NAT in your VPC, HSM KMS integration for keys, and an audit log sink to your SIEM via syslog.

4) Rollout plan: canary on 1 GPU pool (route 10% traffic), smoke tests for latency, model cache warm-up script, automatic fallback to legacy nodes for 72 hours post-cutover.

Action items before call:
- Emma: confirm whether we can use 2 extra 2U slots for one of the GPU pools in Rack B (per your sketch).
- Procurement: we'll share a short SOW + initial hardware SKU list for approval.
- Aditya: bring the node-level latency/IO expectations and a small script to simulate warm cache behavior.

Meeting link: https://meet.redwood.ai/seacliff-onprem (10:00am PT)
Agenda: 1) Review topology + storage sketch (15m), 2) Network/egress & KMS (10m), 3) Rollout/canary plan and fallbacks (10m), 4) Next steps & SOW (10m).

I'll send the draft topology PDF after our call. Looking forward.

Best,
Chloe Martin
